Definition: from G3501 and G4172; new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia:--Neapolis.
BiblicalUsage: Neapolis is the new town where Paul lands after sailing from Troas, on the way to Philippi in Macedonia. The name is written as two words in the Greek, a new city on the shore of the gospel's road into Europe.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the name says what the gospel does: it makes a new town out of an old shore, and Paul's first step into Europe is a step into a place called new.
